title: Multiply Two Polynomials
summary: Given two integer arrays, where each array's element at index i represents the coefficient of x^i in a polynomial, compute the coefficients of the product polynomial R(x) = A(x) × B(x), and return these coefficients in a new integer array of appropriate length.
statement: Given two integer arrays, where each array's element at index i represents the coefficient of x^i in a polynomial, compute the coefficients of the product polynomial R(x) = A(x) × B(x), and return these coefficients in a new integer array of appropriate length.
constraints: Each nonempty array stores coefficients in ascending exponent order.
Use fast convolution rather than multiplying every coefficient pair for large inputs.
reference_solution:
def multiply_polynomials(poly1,poly2):
    import math
    size=len(poly1)+len(poly2)-1;n=1
    while n<size:n*=2
    first=list(map(complex,poly1))+[0j]*(n-len(poly1));second=list(map(complex,poly2))+[0j]*(n-len(poly2))
    def fft(values,invert):
        j=0
        for i in range(1,n):
            bit=n>>1
            while j&bit:j^=bit;bit>>=1
            j^=bit
            if i<j:values[i],values[j]=values[j],values[i]
        length=2
        while length<=n:
            angle=2*math.pi/length*(-1 if invert else 1);root=complex(math.cos(angle),math.sin(angle))
            for start in range(0,n,length):
                factor=1+0j
                for offset in range(length//2):
                    left=values[start+offset];right=values[start+offset+length//2]*factor
                    values[start+offset]=left+right;values[start+offset+length//2]=left-right;factor*=root
            length*=2
        if invert:
            for i in range(n):values[i]/=n
    fft(first,False);fft(second,False)
    for i in range(n):first[i]*=second[i]
    fft(first,True)
    return [round(first[i].real) for i in range(size)]

hints: Polynomial multiplication is convolution: output degree k sums first[i]*second[k-i].
Pad to a power of two, transform both coefficient arrays, multiply pointwise, and apply the inverse transform.
Run iterative bit-reversal FFT, combine spectra, invert, divide by n, and round the real coefficients.
The Fourier transform converts convolution into pointwise multiplication; inverse transformation recovers every coefficient in O(n log n).
